budget.countFirst: Run git diff --numstat <base>...<branch> and git log --oneline <base>..<branch> before reading any hunk. Three dots for git diff (merge-base form, so the diff holds only the branch's own changes), two for git log (the commit range). Record every file with its line counts, and every commit, in the findings document's budget block. A numstat row of - - is a binary file: list it in budget.binaryFiles by path, count it as 0 lines, and never invent a count for it or drop it.
readOrder: files the issue declares under Files to modify
remaining files by diff size ascending
budget.overBudget: A file not read in full because a cap was reached is listed in budget.countedNotRead with its path and line count. It is never silently dropped: the count is evidence, and a non-empty countedNotRead caps the verdict at warn.

criteria.name: Every hunk maps to an acceptance criterion
criteria.description: Each hunk in the range serves at least one of the issue's acceptance criteria, or is flagged as unrelated work.
criteria.check: For each hunk, name the AC it serves. A hunk serving no AC is a finding: unrelated work landing under this issue's Refs #N misattributes it to the gates that key off that commit set.
criteria.evidence: File, hunk header, and either the AC it maps to or the word 'unrelated' with one line saying what the hunk does instead.

criteria.name: No files outside the declared scope
criteria.description: Every changed file is named by the issue's Files to modify declaration or its Files Changed section.
criteria.check: Compare git diff --name-only <base>...<branch> against the declared paths. A changed file the declaration does not name is a finding. Always-protected paths (framework-config.json, framework-manifest.json, .claude/metadata/**, .gh-pmu.json, CHARTER.md) are findings even when a Files Changed section lists them, because only the authored declaration can license them.
criteria.evidence: The undeclared path and the declaration it is absent from.

criteria.name: Tests present for new behavior
criteria.description: New or changed behavior in the range has a test in the same range that exercises it.
criteria.check: For each source hunk that adds or changes behavior, find a test hunk in the range that asserts it. A behavior with no test in the range is a finding; a non-code artifact (spec, JSON, markdown) needs a contract test declaring it as a subject.
criteria.evidence: The source file and line, and either the test file and test name that covers it or the statement that none was found in the range.

criteria.name: Tests are authentic
criteria.description: Tests in the range verify behavior rather than mirror the implementation or assert trivially.
criteria.check: Judge each test in the range by the framework's /bad-test-review criteria, read from .claude/commands/bad-test-review.md at review time. Do not restate those criteria here; a second definition drifts silently from the first.
criteria.evidence: The test file and test name, the /bad-test-review criterion it fails, and the assertion that shows it.

criteria.name: Charter conventions honored
criteria.description: The change uses the tech stack and follows the conventions the project charter declares.
criteria.check: Read the charter's Tech Stack and any conventions it states. A hunk that introduces a dependency, language, or pattern the charter excludes, or ignores a convention it names, is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, and the charter line it conflicts with.

criteria.name: No obvious security faults
criteria.description: The range introduces no hard-coded secret, no string-built query or command from untrusted input, and no unsafe shell invocation.
criteria.check: Scan added lines for credentials, tokens and keys; for SQL, shell or template strings assembled from request or file input without parameterization or escaping; for shell execution with string concatenation or shell: true on user-influenced input; for disabled security defaults.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, and the category (secret, injection, unsafe shell, disabled default).

criteria.name: Every commit carries the expected Refs #N
criteria.description: Each commit in the range references the issue under review.
criteria.check: From git log <base>..<branch>, check that every commit subject or body contains Refs #N for the issue number given as input. A commit without it, or with a different issue number, is a finding.
criteria.evidence: The commit SHA and subject, and the reference it carries or lacks.

criteria.name: Declared spelling policy honored
criteria.description: User-facing text and identifiers follow the spelling policy the charter or project configuration declares, when one is declared.
criteria.check: If the charter or project configuration declares a spelling policy (for example en-GB or en-US), check added prose and identifiers against it. When no policy is declared, emit one pass finding saying so.
criteria.evidence: The file and line, the word, and the policy it breaks.

criteria.name: No debugging leftovers
criteria.description: The range leaves no debug output, breakpoints, commented-out code, or placeholder markers behind.
criteria.check: Scan added lines for console.log and print-style debug output outside logging infrastructure, debugger statements, large commented-out blocks, and TODO, FIXME, XXX or HACK markers that the issue did not ask for.
criteria.evidence: The file and line and the leftover text.

findingsPolicy.perCriterion: Emit at least one finding per criterion. A criterion with no violation emits one pass finding; each violation emits its own finding at the criterion's severity.
findingsPolicy.lineAnchoring: file and line are null only for findings that are not line-anchored, such as a commit message or a whole-range observation.

verdict.warn: Otherwise, any finding with status warn, or a non-empty budget.countedNotRead.

anti-pattern-analysis.whenMissing: Emit one pass finding with criterion anti-pattern/not-installed and continue.
